name: Political Prison Camp No. 14 (Kaechon)

positionSource.title: North Korea's Political Prison Camp, Kwan-li-so No. 14, Update 1
positionSource.publisher: HRNK (Committee for Human Rights in North Korea)

description: Covers 150 square kilometres of a mountainous area near Kaechon City in South Pyongan Province. It appears to have existed since the 1960s and moved to its present location in the early 1980s. All inmates are held for life (UN Commission of Inquiry, A/HRC/25/CRP.1, para. 735).

name: Political Prison Camp No. 15 (Yodok)

positionSource.title: North Korea: Imagery Analysis of Camp 15 "Yodok": Closure of the "Revolutionizing Zone"
positionSource.publisher: HRNK (Committee for Human Rights in North Korea)

description: Spread over about 370 square kilometres covering several valleys in Yodok County. It was divided into a total control zone, whose inmates are held for life, and a revolutionizing zone, from which some prisoners were released (UN Commission of Inquiry, A/HRC/25/CRP.1, para. 735). HRNK's imagery analysis of September 2015 found that the revolutionizing zone's detainee facility was razed in 2013–2014 and is no longer used to house detainees.

name: Political Prison Camp No. 16 (Myonggan, also Hwasong)

positionSource.title: North Korea: Imagery Analysis of Camp 16
positionSource.publisher: HRNK (Committee for Human Rights in North Korea)

description: Covers about 560 square kilometres of rugged terrain in Myonggan, North Hamgyong Province, close to the P'unggye-ri nuclear test site. Witness testimony indicates it has existed since the 1970s, when it was much smaller; inmates live in two settlement areas (UN Commission of Inquiry, A/HRC/25/CRP.1, para. 735).

name: Political Prison Camp No. 18 (Pukchang)

positionSource.title: North Korea's Political Prison Camp Kwan-li-so No. 18 (Pukch'ang)
positionSource.publisher: HRNK (Committee for Human Rights in North Korea)

description: In Bukchang (Pukchang) County, South Pyongan Province, on the south bank of the Taedong River near Camp No. 14. The UN Commission of Inquiry reported in 2014 that it was gradually downsized, that the site was closed in 2006 and that a short-term labour detention facility was placed on its premises (A/HRC/25/CRP.1, para. 739). HRNK's 2024 satellite-imagery report found that smaller sections appear to remain active as a detention facility.

ownerQuestion: The sources differ: the UN Commission of Inquiry (2014, A/HRC/25/CRP.1 para. 739) reported the site closed in 2006; HRNK's newer report (2024) says smaller sections 'remain active as a detention facility'. Under ruling R14b the newest report decides, so the camp keeps its marker and counts as a current crisis, with both statements shown. Approve this, or correct it?
verification: Name and description: A/HRC/25/CRP.1, para. 739 (camps of the Ministry of People's Security until 2006: 'Political Prison Camp No. 18 was gradually downsized until the site in Bukchang ... was closed down in 2006. Today, a short-term labour detention facility has been placed on the premises'). HRNK (report dated June 18, 2024; its web page says 2024-06-23): 'large sections of Kwan-li-so No. 18 were deactivated over a period of at least eight years and ... smaller sections remain active as a detention facility'; 'Whether the official designation of this facility remains Kwan-li-so No. 18 is unknown.' The brief allowed No. 18 if HRNK's 2024 report supports it; it does, but the two sources differ on its status, and the description gives both. Position: HRNK's 'CenterPoint Coordinates: 39.552435 N, 126.073063 E'.

name: Political Prison Camp No. 25 (Chongjin)

positionSource.title: North Korea's Political Prison Camp Kwan-li-so No. 25, Update 4
positionSource.publisher: HRNK (Committee for Human Rights in North Korea)

description: A detention facility near Chongjin City, North Hamgyong Province, with a few thousand prisoners; it looks more like a maximum-security prison, with a main block surrounded by high walls. Its prisoners are held for life without trial on political grounds (UN Commission of Inquiry, A/HRC/25/CRP.1, para. 735).
